I will keep my main land in the wheat-maize rotation because that fits my farm, my well irrigation, and the way I already work. I have 13.1 mu, but some family labor is tied up off-farm, so I will not spread myself too thin with too much cotton. Cotton takes more careful field management and more pesticide work, while wheat and maize are more stable for me and easier to manage on time. So I will put 10.0 mu into winter wheat followed by summer maize on the same 10.0 mu, and I will keep 3.1 mu in cotton. For seed, I will use improved or hybrid seed because I have farmed 15 years and I care more about stable yield than saving on seed. I will use moderate fertilizer because I have irrigation and I want steady growth, not excessive vegetative growth. I will irrigate wheat more than maize and cotton because wheat in my area depends more on timely water at key stages. I will do rotary tillage because it is efficient for my scale and fits how I would manage residue and sowing. I will keep pesticide use moderate: more for cotton, less for wheat and maize, because cotton usually needs closer pest control.
